help.title: HOW TO PLAY
help.body:
You landed at the Moon's south pole. Grow the base until Development reaches 60.

- The Sun stays low and circles the sky in ~10 minutes. Shadows move!
- Solar panels stop in shadow. Batteries cover the dark time.
- Ice hides in the dark crater. Carry it back (watch your suit O2), or build an ice drill there.
- Life support makes water and oxygen from ice. The greenhouse makes food.
- Radiation events: go indoors. Without an Earth link, alerts do not arrive.
- Earth sets for half of each month. Relay satellites keep the link.
help.sources: Data used (values marked TBD are placeholders):
tut.title: Junior Astronaut Training
tut.m1.name: Electricity
tut.m2.name: Radiation
tut.m3.name: Ice and Oxygen
tut.tryAgain: Not quite. Think again and pick another answer!
tut.intro:
Welcome, Junior Astronaut!
You just landed near the Moon's South Pole.

People need 4 things to live here: AIR (oxygen), WATER, FOOD and ELECTRICITY.
Top left shows how many days your air, water and food will last.

Let's learn how to get them, one step at a time!
tut.m1.intro:
Everything in your base runs on electricity, even making air!

The Sun at the Moon's South Pole is strange: it never climbs high in the sky. It slides around the horizon, so hills and mountains throw VERY long shadows.

Look around. Can you see the long shadows?
tut.m1.walkSun:
Walk to the glowing marker. It's a sunny spot.
Move: W A S D keys. Turn the camera: hold the right mouse button and drag.
tut.m1.buildSolar:
Build a solar panel here in the sunshine:
1) Press B to open the build menu
2) Press 2 to choose 'Solar panel' (green preview = sunny)
3) Click or press Enter to place it.
tut.m1.solarLearn:
It works! Your panel makes 10 kW of electricity in sunlight. Look at 'Power' at the top left.

The Sun keeps moving around the horizon, so the shadows move too. Later, your panel may end up in a shadow.
tut.m1.walkShadow:
Now walk to the new marker. It's in a shadow.
Press B and 2 there and look at the preview: it turns YELLOW and says 'In shadow here'. (You don't need to build.) Press B again to close.
tut.m1.quiz: Question: if you put a solar panel here in the shadow, how much electricity will it make?
tut.m1.quizA: The same as in the sunshine (10 kW)
tut.m1.quizC: Double, because it is cool in the shade
tut.m1.quizExplain: Solar panels need direct sunlight. The Moon has no air to spread light around, so its shadows are almost completely dark. In a shadow, a panel makes nothing.
tut.m1.buildBattery: Build a battery: press B, then 3, then click.
tut.m1.batteryLearn:
A battery stores extra electricity while the Sun shines, and gives it back when your panels are in shadow.

See 'Battery' at the top left. Real Moon bases will need batteries too!
tut.m2.intro:
The Sun shoots out tiny, super-fast particles: RADIATION.
On Earth, thick air and Earth's magnetic field protect us. The Moon has neither!

A real instrument on China's Chang'e-4 lander measured about 200 times more radiation on the Moon's surface than on Earth's surface.

'Shielding' at the top left shows how much radiation you got (mSv).
tut.m2.quiz: A big solar storm is coming! Where are you SAFEST?
tut.m2.quizC: Inside a habitat covered with thick Moon dirt (regolith)
tut.m2.quizExplain: Thick, heavy material blocks radiation. Moon dirt piled on a habitat works like a heavy blanket. The lander's thin walls help a little. Outside, you get everything.
tut.m2.buildAntenna:
Build an antenna so Earth can warn you about solar storms:
press B, then 4, then click.
(It works only while Earth is above the horizon.)
tut.m2.antennaLearn:
Connected to Earth! Radio waves take about 1.3 seconds to travel between Earth and the Moon.

Scientists on Earth watch the Sun and send space weather warnings. But at the South Pole, Earth sometimes sinks below the horizon. Then no messages can reach you!
tut.m2.storm:
A space weather alert just arrived from Earth!
This is a replay of a REAL past solar flare.
Choose: go inside, or keep working?
tut.m2.choseShelter: Good choice! Inside, the walls blocked a lot of the radiation.
tut.m2.choseContinue: You kept working outside, so you got the full radiation. Real astronauts go inside during solar storms.
tut.m2.compare:
How much radiation gets through:
- Outside: {0}%
- Inside the lander: {1}%
- Inside a habitat: {2}%
- Habitat covered with regolith: {3}%
tut.m2.waitStorm:
Stay safe until the storm (red bar at the top) is over.
Then press E to go outside.
tut.m3.intro:
Bringing water and air from Earth costs a lot. But the Moon has ICE!

In 2009, NASA's LCROSS mission crashed a rocket stage into a dark crater near the South Pole and found water in the cloud it kicked up.

Let's go get some ice! Watch your suit's oxygen tank (top left). If it runs out, you will be carried back to the lander.
tut.m3.goCrater:
Follow the marker into the dark crater.
(Press Space to jump. The Moon's gravity is only 1/6 of Earth's!)
tut.m3.craterLearn:
You are in a crater where sunlight never reaches the floor.
It is colder than -200 degrees C here, so ice can stay frozen for a very, very long time, maybe billions of years.
tut.m3.collect: Press E to pick up ice.
tut.m3.bringBack:
You've got 20 kg of ice! Carry it back to the lander and press E to go inside.
Keep an eye on your oxygen tank!
tut.m3.buildLifeSupport:
Press E to go outside. Then build Life support near the lander:
press B, then 5, then click.
tut.m3.quiz: Life support makes oxygen from ice. What else does it need?
tut.m3.quizExplain:
Life support melts ice into water. Then it uses electricity to split water (H2O) into hydrogen and oxygen (O2), the air you breathe. This is called ELECTROLYSIS.

Electricity, water and air are all connected!
tut.done:
Training complete! Now it's YOUR base.

Goal: raise 'Development' to 60.
- Keep enough air, water and food.
- Watch out for shadows and solar storms.
- Build a Greenhouse for food, an Ice drill in the crater, and order supplies from Earth (L key).

Press H any time for help.
